ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there is a positively charged water molecule separated from the organic molecule, which can be regarded as [OH3+]; on the right side there is an ester-group fragment containing CO2R2, and it is connected to an adjacent carbon chain. After ignoring all curved arrows, the organic skeleton can be read as R2O-C(=O)-C(R1)-C(R)(NH2)(OH). Reasoning: According to the specified method, write the R2 side as a wildcard ester fragment *OC(=O)-; continue from the carbonyl carbon to the adjacent carbon bearing R1, written as C(*); then to the next carbon bearing R, NH2 and OH, written as C(*)(N)O; finally connect the independent [OH3+] with a dot. Therefore the SMILES is *OC(=O)C(*)C(*)(N)O.[OH3+].

method.method_draft: First transcribe only the atom-bond graph from the image, ignoring all curved arrows. Encode the right-side CO2R2 group as an ester fragment with the R2 side represented by wildcard '*', giving *OC(=O)-. Continue from the carbonyl carbon to the adjacent carbon that also bears R1, so write C(*). Continue to the next carbon bearing R, NH2, and OH, so write C(*)(N)O. Finally add the separate positively charged water molecule as [OH3+] after a dot. The resulting SMILES is *OC(=O)C(*)C(*)(N)O.[OH3+].

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Single direct graph-to-SMILES route: identify the molecular connectivity in the drawing while explicitly ignoring curved arrows, then encode substituent labels as wildcard atoms and the separate protonated water as a disconnected SMILES component.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the drawing as a transition-state structural formula: a separate H2O/H species bearing a positive charge on oxygen; the main molecule contains an ester/carboxyl group labeled CO2R2 attached to a carbon bearing R1, which is bonded to a neighboring carbon bearing R, NH2, and OH. Curved arrows are present but must not be treated as bonds.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction that the required output is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure and that arrows in the image should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: R, R1, and R2 placeholders become wildcard atoms '*'; an ester fragment CO2R2 can be written as *OC(=O)-; disconnected species are separated by '.'; neutral amine and alcohol are written as N and O with implicit hydrogens; protonated water is written [OH3+].
